question: Which automatic labels account for most unsupported DCs, and are they confined to a few disclosures?
pattern: Panel a partitions 42,646 unsupported DCs and is dominated by boundary distortion (44.9%) and conflation (28.6%); together they comprise 73.5% of unsupported DCs. Contradiction is a very small bar: 42 claims (0.10% of unsupported DCs). Panel b uses 1,798 completed disclosures and shows that the two dominant labels also occur broadly, in 98.6% and 96.5% of completed disclosures. Non-disclosure statements are 15.0% of unsupported DCs but appear in 64.3% of disclosures.
meaning: The main diagnostic burden is distributed across many disclosures, rather than being generated by only a few large claim inventories. The differing bar lengths across panels show why frequency per claim and prevalence per disclosure answer different questions. A category can be a modest share of DCs while appearing in most disclosures.
limits: Panel a categories are mutually exclusive for each DC; panel b categories can co-occur within one disclosure. These are frequencies of automated labels, not validated frequencies of error. The rare contradiction category is especially unsuitable for broad conclusions from one illustrative case.
caption: **Read the figure:** panel a partitions all unsupported DCs; panel b measures label presence in a disclosure, so its bars can sum above 100%. All-DC proportions and exact counts accompany the figure. Counts are descriptive; claims within companies are dependent.
